newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S BALKAN STOPS FLIGHTS FOR 24 HOURS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S BALKAN STOPS FLIGHTS FOR 24 HOURS.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines has cancelled Wednesday's international flights for safety reasons because of threatened strikes by technical staff.
Airline spokesman Viktor Melamed said the decision affected 16 international flights, which the airline hoped to run on Thursday if a settlement could be reached.

"The board of directors has taken such a crucial decision to postpone the flights, some of which are to Frankfurt, London, Moscow and Bangkok, as it could not be sure whether aircraft would be properly checked before their flights," Melamed told Reuters.
The airline's management and the technical staff signed a protocol on Monday agreeing monthly negotiations on payments to compensate for soaring inflation, an airline statement said.
But technical staff said on Tuesday they disagreed with the scheme and threatened individual protests including work stoppages.
Balkan's executive director will continue negotiations with the protesters on Wednesday and if an agreement is reached, the airline will run the cancelled flights on Thursday, Melamed said.
Officials said the airline incurred losses of $50 million last year due to leasing fees, the drastic fall of the lev against the dollar and penalties on overdue payments.
The airline's new management said earlier this year that Balkan needed a complete restructuring to stabilise the company and make it profitable and attractive for potential foreign investors.
